findings.summary: The H6 repair states CI behaviour in the present indicative -- 'CI runs SKIP=check-reviewed so the skip is visible in the log' (also .pre-commit-config.yaml:31-33, and 'CI sets CHECK_RANGE' at :20) -- but there is no .github/ in the tree and M0.7 'GitHub Actions workflow running pre-commit run --all-files' is still todo in the backlog. The behaviour of check-reviewed is now described truthfully; the sentence about who arranges the skip is not.
findings.failure_scenario: The author of M0.7 reads AGENTS.md, sees the SKIP already accounted for, and writes the plain workflow. Two outcomes, both bad: without CHECK_RANGE, check-reviewed prints a green 'ok nothing staged' on every CI run -- verified exit 0 in a fresh worktree -- which is precisely the green line that means nothing this row was written to name; or with CHECK_RANGE set globally to rescue check-test-integrity, check-reviewed takes the range branch and hard-fails every push -- verified exit 1, 'no reviewer verdict for the staged bytes' -- and the next person weakens a gate to get CI green. Fix is one word of mood: 'CI must run SKIP=check-reviewed (M0.7)'.

findings.summary: 'Gates run in delta mode by default ... and print which mode they used', and scripts/lib.sh:49 '⚠️ Every gate PRINTS its mode', citing non-negotiable 4. Only 7 of the 22 scripts in scripts/ reference scoped_files or scope_note; check-portability, check-gate-scope, check-dependency-licenses, check-test-budget, check-tdd and check-reviewed print no mode at all. Not introduced by the H6-H13 edits, carried forward.
findings.failure_scenario: A reader takes a green pre-commit line from check-gate-scope or check-portability as a delta pass and re-runs with GATE_SCOPE=full expecting a stronger statement; the two runs are identical because those gates ignore the variable. A gate author reads lib.sh as a framework contract and assumes mode printing is handled for them.

findings.summary: The no-red-record failure message says 'N new test(s) staged' unconditionally, including in CHECK_RANGE mode where nothing is staged. Observed verbatim in a fresh checkout of the staged tree: '3 new test(s) staged but no red record at .harness/tdd/red.json'.
findings.failure_scenario: An operator debugging the documented CI failure greps git diff --cached, finds it empty, and concludes the gate is broken rather than that red records are gitignored -- the exact confusion the H7 prose was added to remove.

findings.summary: The unconstrained @interface branch is kept 'because the 20k-file corpus run that validated this parser ran WITH it'. The label is honest about the missing test, but it substitutes an unverifiable measurement claim for it: no artifact, count or command for that corpus run exists anywhere in the staged tree.
findings.failure_scenario: A later reader wanting to remove or rework the branch has no way to re-run the evidence, so the branch is immortal by assertion. Naming the command and where its output went, or saying plainly that the run is not reproducible from this tree, costs one line.
